steps.message:
# Freeze store integrity maintenance

Ensure the `TextFileBasedViolationStore` maintains the integrity of its `stored.rules` index and files.

Setting `default.integrity` to `repair` will check the index and folder as they are on disk during initialization, even if the same folder was initialized before. Defaulting to `ignore` which checks nothing.

If an entry points to a path that is not a regular file directly within the folder, it is broken. This also applies if the file name is not a valid path.

If an entry is not broken and its file has no violations it is resolved. Files that only contain line breaks are also resolved.

Entries that point to the same file name are shared, even if nothing exists with that name. If multiple entries point to the same regular file they are also shared. Including through a symbolic or hard link. Even if that file is outside the folder.

The `TextFileBasedViolationStore` will not touch any shared entries or files that no entry points to. If an entry is shared and anything else it will remain shared.

When set to `repair` broken entries will be discarded without touching whatever they point to.

When set to `repair` resolved entries and the file they point to will be discarded. If a resolved entry is a symbolic link the file it points to will be deleted as well.

If using `repair` and saving no violations for a known rule it will forget the rule. Its entry will be removed and its file as well. Unless another entry is sharing that file. In which case only the entry will be removed. Even if it points outside the folder. If using `repair` and saving no violations for an unknown rule nothing will be saved.

If it cannot delete the file of a rule it is forgetting it will fail to save and leave the entry.

steps.message: The diff matches the spec. Last step is documenting the new property in the user guide next to the other store options:

arguments.command:
cd /app; python3 - <<'EOF'
p='docs/userguide/008_The_Library_API.adoc'
s=open(p).read()
old='''# can be set to false to forbid updates of the violations stored for frozen rules
# default is true
freeze.store.default.allowStoreUpdate=false
----

This can help in CI environments to prevent misconfiguration:
For example, a CI build should probably never create a new the violation store, but operate on
an existing one.
'''
new='''# can be set to false to forbid updates of the violations stored for frozen rules
# default is true
freeze.store.default.allowStoreUpdate=false

# can be set to repair to discard broken and resolved rules from the violation store
# default is ignore
freeze.store.default.integrity=repair
----

This can help in CI environments to prevent misconfiguration:
For example, a CI build should probably never create a new the violation store, but operate on
an existing one.

With `freeze.store.default.integrity=repair` the index `stored.rules` and the violation files
are checked as they are on disk every time the violation store is initialized:

* entries of the index that do not point to a regular file directly within the store folder are broken
  and will be discarded without touching whatever they point to
* entries whose violation file contains no violations are resolved and will be discarded together with that file
  (if the violation file is a symbolic link, the file it points to will be deleted as well)
* entries pointing to the same file name or the same regular file (e.g. through symbolic or hard links) are shared
  and will never be touched, neither will files that no entry points to

Furthermore, once all violations of a frozen rule are fixed, the rule will be removed from the store,
i.e. its entry and its violation file (unless the file is shared) will be deleted.
Rules without any violations will not be stored at all.
If such a rule is violated again later, it will be treated like a newly frozen rule.
Repairs are only carried out if `freeze.store.default.allowStoreUpdate` is not set to `false`.
'''
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

steps.message:
I've added `default.integrity` (`ignore` by default, or `repair`) to `TextFileBasedViolationStore`. All 78 tests in the freeze package pass, including 23 new integrity tests and a new concurrency test. SpotBugs and spotless couldn't run because their dependencies aren't cached for offline builds; I checked unused imports by hand and found none. The self architecture tests pass. Nothing is committed.

**What `repair` does:**
- **Initialization:** it re-reads `stored.rules` from disk every time, even if that folder was initialized earlier in the same JVM. Ignore mode keeps the old cached behavior.
- **Broken entries** (the name doesn't point to a regular file directly in the folder, including invalid names, `..`, subpaths, absolute paths, directories and dangling links) are dropped from the index. Nothing they point to is touched.
- **Resolved entries** (the file contains only line breaks, or is empty) are dropped along with their file. If the file is a symlink, the file it points to is deleted too.
- **Shared entries** are left alone. Two entries are shared if they point to the same file name, or to the same regular file through symlinks or hard links, including outside the folder. Files that no entry points to are also never touched.
- **Saving no violations** for a known rule removes its entry, and its file unless the file is shared. If the file can't be deleted, `save` throws `StoreUpdateFailedException` and the entry stays. For an unknown rule, nothing is saved.

The changes are in `TextFileBasedViolationStore.java` and `StoreUpdateFailedException.java`. The new tests are in `TextFileBasedViolationStoreIntegrityTest.java`, with one added to the concurrency test, and the user guide (`008_The_Library_API.adoc`) documents the property.

**Defaults I chose where the spec was silent:**
- **Bad values:** the property is case-insensitive, and an unknown value fails initialization with a message listing the valid ones.
- **`allowStoreUpdate=false`:** repair changes nothing on disk and logs a warning for each entry it would have removed.
- **File can't be deleted during startup repair:** the entry is kept and a warning is logged. Initialization doesn't fail; only `save` fails in that case.
- **Path normalization:** file names are compared after normalizing, so `./a` and `a` count as the same name. This only makes more entries count as shared, which means fewer changes.
- **Empty strings:** saving a list made up only of empty strings counts as saving no violations, because that is how such a file reads back.
- **Locking:** saves to the same folder are now serialized within a JVM, so a repair can't delete a file while another instance is writing to it.

**Decision for you:** when a frozen rule reaches zero violations under `repair`, it is removed from the store. If it is violated again later, `FreezingArchRule` treats it as a new rule and silently freezes the new violations instead of failing the build. That follows from the spec, and I've noted it in the user guide, but you may want to confirm it's acceptable.
